help_topics.title: Understanding which work is offered
help_topics.business_question: Why can two users receive different work?
help_topics.plain_answer: SCALE offers work using the supplied user, warehouse, work profile, locations, containers and feature settings. A work profile is a set of execution rules. Some branches prefer assigned work, apply location/priority order or limit the candidate list. Cart selection can also rewrite instruction sequence, so this procedure must not be run as a read-only diagnostic.

help_topics.title: Understanding work monitor totals
help_topics.business_question: Why are work units, instructions and recently closed work different numbers?
help_topics.plain_answer: A work unit can contain several instructions. The group monitor counts distinct work units for chart groups, sums distinct-unit counts within conditions for its total, and counts instruction rows separately. Recently closed instructions come from active and inactive storage within a rolling one-hour timestamp window. Estimated time is stored planning data, not measured elapsed duration.

help_topics.title: Understanding a work-type drilldown
help_topics.business_question: Why does a work-type chart show only part of the warehouse?
help_topics.plain_answer: The work-type chart is scoped to one warehouse and one work group. It shows distinct work units by type and gives instruction and estimate totals for that same group. An unassigned or missing group value selects work with no group; it does not mean every group.

help_topics.title: Understanding work indicator tiles
help_topics.business_question: Why can a work tile disagree with the chart?
help_topics.plain_answer: Each tile asks a different question: aging work, urgent priority, held work, open/in-process work, or assigned in-process work. It counts distinct work units and evaluates the supplied caution and warning rules separately. The reviewed tiles do not include the chart's detail-instruction restriction, so their counts need not match. A recognized tile returns one row even when its count is zero. An unknown or NULL tile selector returns no result set from these branches; absence of a result is different from an empty work count.

help_topics.title: Understanding inactive work storage
help_topics.business_question: Why can closed work still appear after deactivation?
help_topics.plain_answer: The reviewed deactivation routines copy qualifying closed instructions to inactive storage and remove matching active rows. A combined view reads both locations, so moving a row out of the active table does not necessarily remove it from a monitor. Deactivation here moves work records; it does not perform an inventory movement.

help_topics.title: Understanding grouping and assignment changes
help_topics.business_question: Does adding a work unit to a group also assign a worker?
help_topics.plain_answer: The reviewed group-selection update writes the group number and sequence. It does not assign a worker. help_topics.title: Understanding feature scope in work selection
help_topics.business_question: Can a feature work for one user when its global flag is N?
help_topics.plain_answer: In the reviewed feature resolver, global Y enables the named feature. Global N can still return Y for a matching user override; without one it returns N. semantic_contracts.review_scope: Body-level static contract; transitive application and called-module completeness are separate.
semantic_contracts.purpose: Select candidate warehouse instructions; cart regrouping can also persist sequence changes.
inputs_defaults: Thirteen declared inputs: workUnit nvarchar(50), containerId nvarchar(25), user nvarchar(30), workprofile nvarchar(25), workprofileSequence numeric(5), warehouse nvarchar(25), fromto int, fromLoc nvarchar(25), isSystemDirectedWork bit=0, isCartPickingWork bit=0, groupNumber int, transportContId nvarchar(25), isCcWorkUnit bit=0. Only the three bit flags have declared defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: Several strings use ISNULL-to-empty for branch choice; group checks use both numeric comparisons and ISNULL-to-empty. The table GROUP_NUM is nvarchar(50) while this input is int, so conversion behavior matters.
Missing configuration can leave variables NULL and make comparisons unknown or string concatenation NULL. No complete input-validation contract is enforced here.

The profile-wide SELECT has no sequence predicate or ordering, so multiple detail rows can assign differing values without a deterministic chosen row. The sequence-qualified SELECTs have a narrower scope.

Regroup ORDER_BY/TABLE_FIELD_NAME values become SQL syntax, not bound data parameters. The local regroup table is populated in sequence order, but TOP 1 reads from it have no ORDER BY; do not promise that the configured order is preserved.
output_shape: The final dynamic SELECT returns a branch-dependent instruction projection: instruction/work-unit/item/company identities; quantities/units; source, destination and pick/drop locations/warehouses; grouping/sequence; container, lot, serial/catch-weight and location verification metadata. System-directed branches add assignment, condition, priority and aging fields.
Row numbering is ROW_NUMBER or DISTINCT plus DENSE_RANK over a constant, depending on the feature branch. Numbering does not itself establish the final business ordering.

The top-limited performance branch combines a limited cycle-count key selection and non-cycle-count work with UNION ALL, then applies an outer TOP and order. It is not an unlimited list of every eligible task.

ordered_branches.explanation: If cart picking and not cycle-count work, infer group and sequence from matching transport containers; TOP 1 has no ORDER BY. If sequence is nonpositive and no already-picked detail has zero FROM_QTY, construct sort expressions from WORK_REGROUP_ORDER and dynamically assign ROW_NUMBER values to detail instructions in the group.

Otherwise choose a supplied positive group, or a neutral group condition. If work unit and both container inputs are absent, the non-system-directed initiation predicate is false and location initiation is marked; otherwise match work unit or transport container.

Compare the configured profile zones with the relevant ZONE subset. Read profile-wide grouping/initiation/to-assignment/multiple-unit values separately from sequence-qualified work types and from-assignment/container behavior; read delimiter settings and user authorization.

Build initial pick/putaway order; location initiation or system-directed picking can replace it with assignment-method order. A feature branch adds instruction ID as a tie breaker; another changes priority ordering to favor the specified user within priority.

Read the configurable top-row cap with TRY_CAST. Missing, nonnumeric or nonpositive cap becomes 2000. Determine source/destination quantity predicate and warehouse authorization branches from fromto and work-process context. Values other than 0, 1 or 2 have no documented validation branch.

Prepare zone, company, work-type, container, hold, condition, catch-weight and assignment predicates. For the gated system-directed location path, probe minimum priority and user assignment when applicable; then choose exact location, greater location or lower location in that order.

Create the local work-type table by splitting the configured work types. Build one of non-system-directed, system-directed performance/top-limited, performance/non-top, or legacy system-directed SELECTs; project branch-specific location/container metadata.
Execute the final SQL through sp_executesql with separately bound work unit, work types, user, warehouse, profile, container, source location, group and transport container parameters.

semantic_contracts.status_and_quantity_effects: The cart regroup branch writes WORK_INSTRUCTION.SEQUENCE. Candidate SELECTs do not themselves decrement inventory or complete work. No current work record was read.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: WORK_PROFILE_DETAIL, profile plus supplied sequence, work-profile zones, user/company/warehouse access and feature function results affect selection. Effective settings were not fetched.

Feature gates select complete SQL paths; they are not proven enabled by function existence. The row-cap fallback is 2000, not an observed configuration value. No universal sort order follows from AIM examples.
The variable receiptSequenceOrder is assigned but is not subsequently referenced in the captured body; no behavioral effect is attributed to it.
error_and_return_handling: No TRY/CATCH, explicit RAISERROR/THROW, dedicated status return or own rollback is present. Dynamic compilation, invalid configured identifiers, scalar-subquery cardinality and conversion errors can propagate. No execution was attempted.
semantic_contracts.transaction_ownership: No explicit transaction, commit, rollback, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced by this body; caller/session semantics remain authoritative.
concurrency: The group inference, picked-work check, resequencing and final selection are separate statements without a body-owned transaction or explicit reservation lock. Static selection is not proof of exclusive assignment or race-free execution.

Ordering can have ties in branches without the instruction-ID tie breaker; joining descriptive/location/container data can affect row cardinality. No runtime equivalence of performance and legacy branches is claimed.
semantic_contracts.trigger_behavior: The observed WORK_INSTRUCTION trigger is AFTER INSERT; the selector performs UPDATE for regrouping, so that trigger is not directly activated by this operation.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: Application caller, permission enforcement, claim/reservation, picking confirmation and caller transaction are not captured by this body.
Feature names and configuration values were not exposed. Full business-code enumeration and branch-equivalence validation remain separate review work.
Private SQL inspection establishes fixed base-table targets and SQL structure; arbitrary configured sort expressions prevent treating every possible generated statement as validated.

semantic_contracts.purpose: Build work-group chart plus monitor summary counts.
inputs_defaults: filterCriteria nvarchar(MAX), culture nvarchar(10); no defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: Absent warehouse leaves the local variable NULL, so warehouse comparisons match no rows. Duplicate matching filter names are assigned without ordering.

Empty matching work produces an empty chart; outer SUM values for work units, instructions and condition counts can be NULL, while estimated-time ISNULL gives zero and the closed COUNT gives zero. COUNT(DISTINCT WORK_UNIT) excludes NULL work-unit values.

A work unit in two conditions contributes to both per-condition distinct counts; the summed unit total is not a warehouse-wide distinct count. A NULL group gets localized category text but NULL description.
output_shape: Seven result sets: chart rows with binding/category/data/description/axis/drilldown/title fields, followed by six one-row scalar result sets for units, instructions, estimated time, open, in-process and recently closed instructions.

ordered_branches.explanation: Parse filter text and assign warehouse.
Read nonclosed detail instructions in either source or destination warehouse; join work-group description, group by work group and description, count distinct work units, order by count descending.
Group nonclosed detail instructions by condition, sum per-condition distinct units and instruction counts, estimated time and open/in-process instruction counts.
Count closed detail instructions in WORK_INSTRUCTION_VIEW whose stamp is at or after UTC now minus one hour. Return the six scalars after the chart.

semantic_contracts.status_and_quantity_effects: No stored quantities or statuses are changed by this body.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: GENERIC_CONFIG_DETAIL descriptions and culture-dependent resources affect presentation. Its identifier join followed by a record-type WHERE condition can exclude work when only other record-type matches exist; duplicate descriptions can split chart groups.
error_and_return_handling: SET NOCOUNT ON/OFF; normal explicit RETURN 0 and a final @@ERROR/GOTO handler. This single late check is not comprehensive handling of every prior statement; errors can propagate before it.
semantic_contracts.transaction_ownership: No explicit transaction, commit, rollback, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced by this body; caller/session semantics remain authoritative.
concurrency: Chart, totals and recent-closed count are separate queries without a common snapshot transaction in the body. Concurrent changes can make the result sets disagree even with identical filters.
semantic_contracts.trigger_behavior: No persistent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE in this body; no DML trigger is activated by its reads.
